Existing equipment supplies its actual price, mass and container capacity. Scribe's supplies use Calligrapher's supplies, as already reviewed. **New binding:** Tailor's tools use Weaver's tools; needles and shears are ordinary durable implements of that kit, while a loom/cutting table remains a separate station. Skinning's listed implements are grouped into the new Skinner's tools credential and kit. Fishing tackle is a permissible particular tool proficiency when a grant allows any tool; it is not an artisan-tool choice. The other non-artisan categories likewise do not become artisan tools just because a character has an artisan choice.

Arcana tools, religious implements, divination tools, survival tools, siege engineer tools, carpenter tools and unrelated proficiencies do not automatically substitute for one of these primary credentials. Explicit grants keep their actual scopes. They may support a plausible task without conferring a separate crafting trade.

# Common equipment procedures

**REVIEWED authored operational PLAYTEST equipment/acquisition scope.** These new procedures complete source item names and prices under the [equipment guide](EQUIPMENT_ACQUISITION_PLAYTEST.md). They do not claim to reproduce missing Player-book effect text. Use the complete [source tables](EQUIPMENT_SOURCE_BINDINGS.md) for costs, weights and bundles.

Unless stated otherwise, using a consumable requires an Action, one available hand and access to the actual item. Spend one real unit. Drinking a potion or antitoxin, or feeding one to a willing or Incapacitated living creature within 5 feet, takes an Action. Inability to swallow blocks an oral dose. This gives no free way to dose an unwilling active creature. A potion, poison and healer's kit are not spells.

## Medicine and alchemy

| Item | Procedure |
|---|---|
| Basic Potion of Healing | Drink or feed to restore 2d4 + 2 ordinary HP, subject to actual healing blockers and caps. No Wound removal, resurrection, resource refill or stabilization of a Dead target. |
| Antitoxin | Drink or feed for advantage on saves against poison for one elapsed hour. It grants no immunity, automatic cure or advantage on unrelated CON saves. A new dose uses the later expiry without stacking advantage. |
| Healer's kit | A full 5-gp, 3-lb kit has ten consumable charges. Action and one charge automatically stabilize an adjacent living dying creature under the reviewed Core rule. Other medical procedures retain their own time, checks and charge costs. No universal HP healing. |
| Acid vial | Action: ranged improvised attack against one perceived creature or object within 20 feet, using DEX and PB only when actually eligible. Hit: 2d6 acid, with no ability damage. The vial is consumed hit or miss, with no splash or persistent acid pool. |
| Alchemist's fire | Use the same 20-foot Action attack as acid. A hit applies reviewed Burning at 1d4 fire, with no immediate damage. Its missing source DC uses the existing DC 10 fallback. Burning's family arbitration, regular-end pulses, saves and extinguishing procedures apply. Another flask does not create a second simultaneous winning fire-family pulse. |
| Holy water | Action: the same 20-foot ranged improvised attack, or a splash attack against one adjacent target. Hit: 2d6 radiant only if the target actually has Fiend or Undead type. The active Undead ancestry has that type. The flask is consumed even against an ineligible target. No inferred type from appearance or religious affiliation, and no extra exorcism. |
| Basic poison | Action: coat one piercing/slashing weapon or up to three compatible piercing/slashing ammunition units with one dose. For one elapsed minute, the first qualifying weapon hit, or first hit by each coated ammunition unit, forces DC 10 CON: failure takes 1d4 poison, success zero. That coating is then spent. No Poisoned condition. Coatings do not stack; expiry or washing ends them. |

Each coated ammunition unit keeps its own one-hit entitlement until used or expiry. Missing does not itself remove the coating, although firing still expends the ammunition normally. Recovery and physical integrity still apply.

## Examples

An alchemist's-fire hit applies a Burning record. At the creature's regular end, it offers its 1d4 fire through existing family arbitration; the normal ending save follows due ticks. Another ordinary attached fire may win instead. Spending the existing extinguish Action clears ordinary-extinguishable attached fires without an invented extra check.

A poisoned arrow that misses still physically exists wherever it lands. Its coating persists only until the original one-minute deadline and needs a legal physical recovery before another use. Recovering it does not refresh the poison or create a second arrow.

## Shared handling

This overlay governs generic conditions in the combined candidate. A reviewed card overrides a generic clause only where it prints the specific exception. An unreviewed historical summary never grants an extra ability or bypasses a gate. The existing combined source-character/target/encounter hard-denial cap still applies to class/spell/companion applications.

Record each condition source, affected creature, applying DC, magnitude, start, duration and ending method. Same-name nonnumeric penalties apply once; independent sources continue until each ends. A generic cure naming a condition clears its source records unless a reviewed procedure specifies one-record scope. Bleeding Medicine and Burning DEX saves use the specific procedures below. Track Charmed, Frightened, Marked and Grappled relationships separately. Exhaustion, Intoxication, Unity and Wounds use their explicit tracks.

Immunity to a named condition prevents that condition, including an inherited component, but does not silently grant immunity to every parent condition that can cause it. For example, Prone immunity prevents the Prone component of Unconscious, not its other effects. Immunity to an inflicted condition never erases the underlying zero-HP or dead state. Gaining immunity suppresses applicable existing effects while immunity lasts; their clocks continue unless explicitly paused. Removing immunity does not reapply a one-time consequence or restart an old duration.

Advantages and disadvantages never multiply dice: any advantage and any disadvantage cancel to one normal d20 roll, regardless of the number of sources. Automatic failure of a required check/save is resolved without a roll. A condition does not give a save where its source grants none. A critical-if-hit rider never makes a missed attack hit. Automatic failure has no rolled total: use ordinary Failure, not Critical Failure or an invented failure margin, unless the source explicitly supplies one.

Generic Core Bleeding and Burning join family.bleeding and family.ongoing-fire respectively, with source-owner stack groups. At one identical target timing marker, all due generic and custom groups in that family compete: highest expected unmitigated damage, then earliest application. Only the winning group's source-permitted instances deal damage. All due groups consume that tick; losers do not defer or bank it. Different printed markers resolve separately. No record also receives a duplicate generic tick. Core generic timing is end of regular target turn; extra turns do not tick. Outside initiative preserve one periodic step per complete six seconds with no duplicate interval across initiative transitions.

Strain is not globally unique: expedition.strain and warrior.serum-strain are separate source-qualified tracks, both distinct from the six-level Exhaustion condition. See the Strain namespace reference for the current candidate. Oracle one-turn Revelation backlash is also separate from global Exhaustion; its printed penalties and endpoint remain unchanged. Wound Eater feeding failures explicitly use global Exhaustion. Never silently convert similarly named tracks.

See CONDITION_RECOVERY_PLAYTEST.md for finite recovery, cleansing, substance, Intoxication and Unity procedures. These new proposals are labeled separately from recovered source rules. Conditions do not reveal Director secrets or force player beliefs or decisions.

SUPERSESSION — NEW PROVISIONAL INTEGRATION: The unified Bleeding/ongoing-fire family registry supersedes earlier provisional clauses that selected generic records separately, used ending DC as a damage tie-breaker, cleared all generic Bleeding through one Medicine result, or used one Burning save to clear all generic Burning. Original Core quotations and raw review history remain unchanged. See CUSTOM_CONDITION_BINDINGS.md and the recorded GPT_GENERIC_CUSTOM_ALIGNMENT review.

## Burning

**Preserved Core text:** Take fire damage at end of turn. An action, immersion, or successful Dexterity save ends it.

**Effect:** At end of the affected creature's regular turn its generic record offers 1d4 fire damage to unified family arbitration, unless its source specifies another magnitude. Only the winning stack group deals damage. Damage immunity does not by itself remove Burning.

**Application:** Applied only by an effect that explicitly inflicts Burning. Record the applying effect's DC; if none exists, use DC 10.

**Duration and ending:** Self or adjacent helper may spend one Action to end all active ordinary-extinguishable attached fires on this creature. Full immersion of all burning portions does the same. Explicit protected-source exceptions survive. At each regular target turn end, after due ticks are consumed, each surviving active ongoing-fire record with future damage remaining makes its own binary DEX save against its own source DC or 10. Success ends only that record. An indefinite generic fire counts as having future damage; a finite record with its final tick consumed expires without another save.

**Stacking:** Independent records enter unified ongoing-fire family arbitration. One Action/full immersion clears all ordinary-extinguishable records; DEX saves operate per surviving eligible record, not one selected-source save for all fires.

**Immunities and specific exceptions:** Fire immunity prevents the damage but does not automatically end Burning unless the source or immunity says so. An effect explicitly immune to Burning blocks application.

**Explicit integration decisions:**

- NEW: 1d4 fire fallback, source DC or 10, damage then free ending save; Action/immersion can end before damage.
- NEW: shared periodic timing and strongest-record precedence; adjacent helper and immersion boundaries.

## Frightened **Preserved Core text:** Disadvantage while source is visible and cannot willingly move closer. **Effect:** While the source of fear is visible/in line of sight, the creature has disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls. While Frightened it cannot willingly move closer to that source. **Application:** Each application records its fear source. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's duration and repeat-save procedure. **Stacking:** Separate fear sources are tracked independently. Disadvantage does not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Fear immunity blocks application. Forced movement may move the creature closer because the prohibition is on willing movement. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 specifies disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while the source of fear is within line of sight, and prohibits willingly moving closer.

**family.bleeding.** Explicit hostile Bleed classification for immunity, curing and stated eligibility. Class/owner/source timing and caps remain separate. No inherited damage package.

**family.ongoing-fire.** Only explicitly registered creature-attached Burn-style periodic fire. Excludes direct fire, areas, hazards, environmental flames, object ignition, Resonance Burn and names alone.

**periodic.arbitration.** Generic Core and custom groups enter ONE family arbitration at an identical target marker. Within each family at one identical target timing marker, select one stack group by highest expected unmitigated damage then earliest application. Apply source instance caps before comparing. All due groups consume their tick, including non-damaging losers. Different markers and families resolve separately. Stable unique application sequence breaks simultaneous applications in resolution order; lexical group ID is a final implementation tie-break only.

**ownership.** Ordinary your means ownerCharacterId. Explicit class phrases restrict sourceClass. Crimson technical Bleed engine hooks require owned Crimson instances. Suppressed, immune, inactive or expired effects do not satisfy active-effect hooks.

**hp-cure-separation.** HP prohibition prevents regained HP. Legal positive-potential magical healing can still invoke a registered Bleed cure, including Blood Curse CON save; a remover explicitly requiring actual HP gained retains that prerequisite.

**exclusive-periodic-binding.** A textual effect component with a reviewed source-qualified profile creates only that record. Core Bleeding/Burning are fallback identities only for explicit Core applications lacking a more-specific profile. A family tag or display word never also creates a generic record. Two records require two effects explicitly imposed by the operative source.

**immunity-and-periodic-arbitration.** Condition/family immunity prevents initial application. Gained condition/family immunity suppresses an existing record: clocks and due ticks continue, but suppressed records are excluded from damage arbitration and active-effect hooks. Damage-type immunity/resistance does not suppress the record or exclude it from arbitration; choose using unmitigated expectation, then apply defenses.

**recipe-occupancy.** A poison recipe occupies an ongoing-instance slot only while at least one ongoing component remains. Suppression does not erase an existing component; curing/expiry can end it. Resolved one-time critical healing does not occupy a slot. Ending Bloodleech's sole remaining Bleed ends its occupancy without purging other poison or curse records.

**cure-presence-suppression.** SUPERSESSION: Cure/removal tests existing unexpired presence, not current effect activity. Medicine selects one present eligible Bleed; positive-potential legal magical healing invokes each present eligible endpoint (Blood Curse retains CON save); Action/full immersion ends all present ordinary-extinguishable fires. Suppression/acquired condition immunity does not bar these cures or existing permitted ending saves. Damage arbitration and active-effect hooks still exclude suppressed/immune records. Initial immunity prevents new application; ended records cannot resume.

**Application records.** Preserve application ID, owner character, source class/engine, target, DC, damage type, start, remaining ticks or expiry, source stack group, and cure exceptions. “Immune” in an active-effect eligibility check means immunity to the condition/application, not merely immunity to its damage type. Damage immunity does not by itself erase an effect.

**Timing.** Explicit start/end timing wins. An omitted next-turn periodic marker is provisionally end of the next regular target turn. Extra turns add no periodic ticks or ending saves. Outside initiative preserve the clock and consume one due step per complete six seconds; initiative transitions do not duplicate events.

**Bleed treatment.** A WIS (Medicine) Action by self or an adjacent helper selects one ordinary Bleed record before rolling: printed cure DC, otherwise recorded applying effect/class/spell DC, otherwise 10. Success ends that record. One legal magical-healing event with positive pre-cap/pre-prohibition potential ends every eligible automatic-healing-cure record; each Blood Curse instead receives its own CON save. An explicit remover keeps its stated one/all/owner scope.

**Cure presence.** Treatment, magical-healing cure and permitted per-record ending saves can remove a still-present suppressed or condition-immune Bleed/fire record. Cure scope and special prerequisites remain unchanged. Effect eligibility and damage arbitration still exclude suppressed records. Successful removal ends the record permanently; immunity ending cannot restore it.

**Kit exceptions.** A Crimson kit Action consumes one use and ends that source owner's Crimson Bleeds on the victim. A Dragoon kit Action consumes one use and ends the selected Dragoon Bleed. Other records do not silently acquire these kit endpoints.

**Attached fire treatment.** One self/helper extinguish Action or full immersion ends all ordinary-extinguishable attached fires on that creature. Explicit protected-fire exceptions survive. At the end of each regular target turn, after due ticks are consumed, each still-active fire record with future ticks remaining receives its own ending DEX save at its source DC or 10. An indefinite generic fire has future ticks. No ending save is needed after a record's final tick expires.

**Duration changes.** Printed base duration is distinct from an express hard cap. A qualifying refresh never shortens remaining duration. Persistent Bleed normally supplies two turns; Prolonged Suffering changes application/refresh to four only for owned profiles whose printed base is exactly two. Use the greatest legal replacement, not a sum; obey actual hard caps. No source trigger means no refresh, and expired records cannot be refreshed.

### Dread — `oracle.dread`

-1 attack rolls and saving throws. Any Reaction denial is a separately timed rider.

**Immunity:** Explicit family immunity applies only to the registered family. Damage resistance/immunity uses the actual damage type. An immune or suppressed record cannot satisfy active-effect hooks.

**Tags:** No shared family tag.

Internal poison-recipe delayed fire; explicitly excluded from family.ongoing-fire. Can coexist with a Burn-family tick.
Poison damage immunity blocks poison damage only; Core Poisoned immunity blocks only actual Poisoned components. Explicit immunity to poison effects/toxins is checked separately against the application.
Failed recipe save still required; critical no-HP-recovery ends end next regular turn separately from the two-tick fire.
One recipe instance per owner/target and maximum two different ongoing poison recipes from that owner.

**Exact cure metadata:**

```json
{
  "ordinaryExtinguishable": false,
  "corePoisonedRemovalApplies": false,
  "underlyingPoisonRemoval": "Only an explicitly reviewed cure covering active poison recipe effects can remove remaining recipe riders.",
  "expiry": "Two scheduled ticks; recipe can be refreshed under Thief engine rules.",
  "presenceRule": "Existing unexpired/not-ended record, including suppressed/condition-immune records. Actual cure method/endpoint/prerequisites still required."
}
```

Noncombat helpers cannot attack or operate combat items.

A cantrip that stabilizes restores no HP and removes no Wound. Mending cannot replace finite machine repair or refresh ammunition, charges, duration or class resources. Created tools, servants and water obey the explicit card limits; a spell does not silently pay wages, produce saleable materials or erase abstract expedition Supply.

All hard whole-Action/turn denial uses one combined **source-character/target/encounter** record across that character's spells, class features and companions. Once used, later hard-denial riders from that source fail; damage and soft riders resolve as printed. Boss immunities remain effective. Same-stat flat bonuses use the strongest; same-name dice bonuses do not stack. Apply one allowed bonus-die spell per roll in this packet unless a reviewed feature explicitly permits more. Temporary HP never add together. Copies never generate copies, class procs or resource loops.
